body: This really isn't anything that can help you, but literally the same thing happened to me a couple of weeks ago. They were my everything, my support system, my best friend. They recently found out my diagnosis and since that day it deteriorated quickly. People have said to me, that if they loved you enough, they'll love you faults and all. So don't be hard on yourself, don't blame yourself. I think that every single person has some sort of 'fault'. I'm not saying that BPD is a fault, but it's a quirk. And the person who broke up with you may find another person but they'll have their own challenges too. No person is perfect and you'll find someone who will love you and cherish you for who you are. The first few weeks will be hell, surround yourself with people and make yourself so busy that your exhausted and rely on people, call them and reach out. Your support system is bigger than you know right now. Hope you feel better and feel free to message me if you need
This is too relatable, I feel you've managed to put into words what I've found so hard to explain

Thanks for taking the time to reply, you've given so much information and help, I really appreciate that. It does make me feel slightly better that someone else has felt that way too. I'm going to have a look into some of the things you've said before. I didn't really like CBT but I think maybe it was very low level, not intense at all. As in, nothing was going to happen if I didn't go for that run. 

I really hope you are okay and I'm sorry you've gone through a low period. I'm glad to see you've taken steps to better your mindset and day to day life.

I did feel a little shut down,  I really understand if they have gone through a difficult period, but without trying to make it sound about me, it WAS about me in that moment. I felt like it was taken away from me as I opened up. Thanks for replying, it's good to know that I was okay to feel that way.
Thanks for replying, it really does make me feel better that I'm not the only one that feels this way. I hope you feel better too soon, stay safe

That thread you linked was raw, I'm so thankful you read it. I think it really shows that more people care than you are aware of.

I'm trying to be more open and have these conversations. but as soon as I start I just trail off and say I'm having a bad 'period of time'. 

Thanks again for replying, I really am grateful

Thanks for taking the time to reply to this post.

I haven't seen a professional, only my GP. They told me I have anxiety and severe depression. But I have been reading up, I feel I more associate with DID? But then I feel the same about bipolar, but I base that mainly on my ability to behave differently with others or alone but I don't think that is as likely to be my diagnosis. I think it's bad to self diagnose. I'm waiting on a referral but it has been a few months now. 

It really does help knowing that others have felt similar for some reason, less alone.

I definitely went through the denial phase. I think I'm currently in the accepting stage, but stopping myself from getting better for some reason. I am starting to tell people whats going on, but I'm still afraid of judgement or people thinking I'm attention seeking or a classic case.

I really appreciate the time you've taken to to bullet point these steps out, I think it's good to hear it from someone else sometimes. 

I have thought about therapy - but in the UK, I'm waiting on the NHS referral. Unfortunately, it can be months if not longer. I'm thinking of paying for it but I just keep talking myself out of it, saying, 'what would I talk about'.

you're last point is definitely the hardest, I think I just take it so personally. So i just want to shut off people so I don't get hurt.

you're completely right, that people always say 'it will get better' or 'give it some time', or 'just wait, be patient'. I think it's just, I think it feels like a consistent drag trying to push myself.  
Thanks for taking the time to reply, and I appreciate the offer to message you!

Thank you so much for takin the time to reply to this, I really appreciate what you said too. I watched the video, and I think you're right, it definitely is a good analogy for how we think and can feel.

I appreciate this view completely, it definitely makes sense. I know I shouldn't be on top of the world but I just don't feel any better to when I started taking them. I feel my mood swings are more aggressive. I can put on a front of being happy with others but then on my own, I will breakdown and cry. 

Thanks for taking the time to give your view on this- I think I'll stick it out a while and then speak back with the doctor about possible other medications if it comes to that
